final_answer:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689) Gap Analysis, Vantage Mobility Solutions GmbH
To: Dr. Katrin Weiss (CCO); cc T. Engel (GC). Prepared for the 31 March 2025 Management Board session. Basis: seven supplied documents; statutory text checked only via secondary sources (EUR-Lex and the AI Act Service Desk were blocked), so article pinpoints marked [verify] need confirmation against the OJ text.

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) The internal working summary (20 Jan 2025) and questionnaire contain classification and legal errors that change the plan. Reg. 2019/2144 (General Safety Regulation) and Reg. 2018/858 sit in Annex I Section B, not Section A. Under Art. 2(2), for Section B only Art. 6(1), Arts. 102-109 and Art. 112 apply. PathNav/PedDetect therefore do not face direct Chapter III, Art. 43 or Art. 47 obligations. AI Act requirements reach them through delegated/implementing acts under the type-approval regime. The "notified body EUR 200-350k vs Annex VI internal control" question is therefore mis-framed; the real conformity route is type-approval. Whether such acts have been adopted is unresolved.
(b) FleetScore is probably not Annex III high-risk. Annex III point 5(b) is creditworthiness/credit scoring; 5(c) is risk assessment and pricing for life and health insurance. Motor/fleet insurance is in neither. The summary mis-letters these (calls life/health 5(b), credit 5(a)); Dr. Roth's "5(b)" label is also unsupported. Even so, FleetScore carries serious non-AI-Act exposure (age bias, GDPR, non-disclosure to NovaStar) and should be remediated now.
(c) PredMaint is probably not high-risk, but the conclusion must be documented.
(d) Penalty exposure is understated. Art. 99 caps for undertakings are the HIGHER of the fixed sum or percentage: EUR 35m (Art. 5), EUR 15m (other operator obligations), EUR 7.5m (incorrect information), not EUR 23.8m/10.2m/3.4m as the summary computes [verify].
(e) The most urgent items are non-deadline-driven: FleetScore age bias (known since 3 Sep 2024, five months, unmitigated, undisclosed), the Rotterdam near-miss, and 72-hour logs.
(f) Currentness (today 2 Oct 2026): secondary sources report the Digital Omnibus on AI entered into force 27 Jul 2026, deferring Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 Dec 2027 and Annex I-embedded systems to 2 Aug 2028 (Orrick, Gibson Dunn, DLA Piper summaries; OJ text not read). The 2 Aug 2026/2027 dates in the documents are therefore superseded; confirm and re-baseline. Remediation remains necessary.

2. CLASSIFICATION AND ROLE (all systems: Vantage is provider, Art. 3(3); EU-established; NovaStar, Swiss, is a deployer whose output is used in the Union, Art. 2(1)(c))
PathNav v3.2 / PedDetect v4.0: safety components (Art. 3(14)) of Level 3 vehicles under Section B legislation. Art. 6(1) is listed as applicable but substantive requirements arrive via vehicle-law acts (Arts. 104, 109 amend 2018/858 and 2019/2144). Practical advice: still build to Arts. 9-15 and 17 because those become the type-approval benchmark and the OEM contractual ask; do not budget a notified body under the AI Act on the present premise; confirm with the approval authority/technical service for the November 2025 v3.3 submission. Annex VI cannot be assumed either way.
FleetScore v2.1: see 1(b). Art. 6(3) profiling carve-back would deny any derogation if Annex III applied. Annex III can be amended (Art. 7) and Commission guidelines (Art. 6(5)) may widen interpretation; monitor.
PredMaint v1.8: not integrated in the vehicle, advisory, human-reviewed (Art. 14 workflow already exists). Annex III point 2 covers safety components in management/operation of road traffic infrastructure, not fleet maintenance software; the summary's Area 2/Recital 47 theory is a stretch. Facts cutting the other way: alerts cover brakes, steering, tyres; recall 96.8% on safety components. Keep as not high-risk with a written rationale; product-liability exposure remains (Directive (EU) 2024/2853 treats software as a product for products placed on market after 9 Dec 2026 [verify]).
Art. 4 AI literacy applies from 2 Feb 2025 to all four systems; the summary omits it. The summary's cites to "Art. 52" transparency are pre-final numbering (now Art. 50). Art. 10(5) (special-category data for bias detection) is irrelevant to age, which is not a special category.

3. ART. 5 SCREEN (applies since 2 Feb 2025; fines apply from 2 Aug 2025)
FleetScore: Art. 5(1)(c) social scoring requires scoring of social behaviour or personality characteristics leading to unrelated-context or disproportionate detriment. Driving telematics used for motor pricing is same-context; low risk. Conditions: contractually bar NovaStar from reuse in credit, housing, employment or other contexts; test proportionality. Art. 5(1)(b) (age vulnerability exploitation) not engaged: no behavioural distortion. Others N/A.

4. REQUIREMENT-BY-REQUIREMENT GAPS (P=PathNav, F=FleetScore, D=PedDetect, M=PredMaint). Status uses the questionnaire's scale; "benchmark" means standard if/when imported.
Art. 9 risk management: P, D partial (ISO 26262 lacks AI risks: bias, drift, adversarial). F none; quarterly informal reviews; age bias never risk-assessed. M: failure-mode analysis stale (12 Jun 2023). Fix: extend ISO 26262 process with AI risk taxonomy (ISO/IEC 23894 per Pinnacle); F formal process.
Art. 10 data governance: P 62% Germany, 15% Netherlands, 3% eight states; representativeness gap (Art. 10(3)-(4)) for deployment elsewhere. D: CityScapes-Extended (3.1m frames) has no provenance and was used under an academic/research licence; confirm commercial-use rights (licence risk, not only data quality); SensorLab (1.7m) has no annotation or bias warranties; about 40% of frames lack Vantage provenance; low-light cyclist frames under 4%. F: no bias examination (Art. 10(2)(f)-(g)); NovaStar claims data includes age band; data used without validation. 
Art. 11/Annex IV documentation: P type-approval file (about 450 pp) lacks AI content; D none standalone; F 12-page spec only; M 4-page README. Fix: Annex IV files; PredMaint only if reclassified.
Art. 12 logging / Art. 19 retention (six months minimum for provider-controlled logs [verify]): P/D 72 hours; F no individual logs, and the NovaStar package says individual scores are not stored; M 18 months (adequate). Cost: current EUR 43k/month for 72 hours; the engineering document puts 30 days at about EUR 430k/month; linear extrapolation to six months is about EUR 2.6m/month in steady state, exceeding the whole EUR 1.3m budget. Raw sensor retention is not what Art. 12 requires; design event-triggered logging (inferences, confidences, takeovers, near-misses, system state), tiered storage and compression. The Rotterdam data survived only because an engineer copied it manually.
Art. 13 instructions for use: P integration manual omits limitations, bias, oversight; D 99.2% disclosed but 91.7% (low light) and 87.3% (heavy rain/snow) not disclosed to OEMs, a known Art. 13(3)(b)(ii)-(iii)/Art. 15(2) item and potential misleading-information exposure; F brochure/API guide only; no limitations, no age-bias disclosure.
Art. 14 human oversight: P Level 3 driver fallback only; no AI-layer override, interrupt or remote console; assess against Art. 14(4)(d)-(e) as benchmark; D same. F auto-applied premiums, no review; the automation-bias risk (Art. 14(4)(b)) applies only if high-risk, but deployer-side review is good practice and GDPR Art. 22 relevant [verify applicability, as premium payers are fleet operators]. M adequate human-in-loop.
Art. 15 accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity: P/D no adversarial ML testing (patches, LiDAR spoofing, poisoning), unscheduled; D combined-condition benchmarks absent. F R2 0.71 (AUC 0.84), no subgroup, robustness or security work. Fix: schedule adversarial testing before v3.3 submission.
Art. 17 QMS: ISO 9001 (QMS-2023-04812, valid to 31 Dec 2026, so renewal falls inside the programme) lacks AI procedures (data, training/testing, change management, PMM, incident reporting, accountability). Extend;
Art. 43/47/48/49: nothing initiated. Per 1(a): P/D via type-approval; Art. 49 registration applies to Annex III systems, not Annex I; the summary's Art. 49(3) is unsupported [verify]. F: if ever Annex III, Annex VI and registration apply.
Art. 72 post-market monitoring: P/D vehicle surveillance lacks drift/bias/AI metrics; F none, no deployer feedback channel; M informal quarterly review.
Art. 73 serious incidents / Art. 3(49): no AI procedure. See section 6.
Art. 26/27 deployers: NovaStar has not been told of obligations. If FleetScore is outside Annex III, Art. 26 and Art. 27 (FRIA only for Annex III 5(b)-(c) deployers) fall away; the summary's "5(a)/(b)" trigger is mis-lettered. Provide NovaStar information voluntarily regardless.

5. FLEETSCORE AGE BIAS (central)
Facts: under-25s scored 8-12 points lower (higher assumed risk) than behaviourally matched drivers (18-24 mean 58.3 vs 67.1 for 35-44, gap 8.8); 25-34 about 4-6 points. Root cause is probably the claims labels. Documents are inconsistent: the email went to Hoffstadt and Weiss (so Legal/Compliance knew from 3 Sep 2024), but engineering says it went to the team lead; engineering calls it a "routine review", the email an initiative; Pinnacle writes "lower risk scores", ambiguous because 0 = highest risk.
Analysis: not an Art. 10 breach if FleetScore is not high-risk, but: GDPR fairness/accuracy and Art. 22/automated profiling; German AGG age-discrimination exposure for insurance pricing (actuarial justification under AGG s.20 cannot cover a score that exceeds what behaviour justifies) [verify]; contract/UWG exposure because the NovaStar brochure claims continuous monitoring, equitable pricing and "reward safe driving". The planned Q1 2025 retraining on the same labels would replicate the bias.
Actions: litigation hold and privileged investigation now (3-4 week bias audit); remove age-proxy features and test fairness metrics before retraining; disclose to NovaStar promptly (decision for GC); consider price remediation; fix documentation.

6. ROTTERDAM NEAR-MISS (IR-2024-0847)
Final Art. 3(49) defines serious incident as one that "directly or indirectly leads" to death/serious harm, etc.; the summary's "might have led" language and Art. 3(24) number reflect the earlier draft [verify]. No harm occurred, so a near-miss is likely not a reportable serious incident, and Art. 73 and Chapter III are not yet applicable; Art. 2(8) excludes pre-market testing. However: (i) the identical PedDetect is in production vehicles with a known low-light weakness and 0.45 threshold; (ii) vehicle-law notification duties (type-approval defect/serious risk, GPSR) must be assessed now by the Quality and Regulatory Affairs team, which was bypassed; (iii) the test ran on a public road, so check RDW/KBA test-permit incident conditions; (iv) the report (preservation, 2.1 m stop at 32 km/h, 14 missed frames) is the evidence for Art. 9 risk. Interim Art. 73 procedure needed: 15 days general, 10 for death, 2 for widespread infringement or critical infrastructure [verify].
Record inconsistencies to reconcile before any external use: location (facility's operational area vs public Route RT-07 1.2 km away); safety driver (Tobias Klinger vs Pieter van Dijk); author (de Vries, 18 Oct vs Meier/Roth, 22-24 Oct); the stated sunset of 17:18 appears early for Rotterdam on 17 Oct (verify; if wrong, "civil twilight" and 15-20 lux need checking); classification "Moderate" vs "Near-Miss".

7. OTHER DOCUMENT INCONSISTENCIES (supervisor flags)
PredMaint: questionnaire says retrained quarterly with data Jan 2018-Mar 2024; engineering says last retrained June 2023, data 2017-2023, and newer sensors unrepresented. Munich address: Leopoldstrasse 142 vs Karlstrasse 42. FleetScore package dated Feb 2024 cites FY2024 revenue; scoring is described as real-time (15 minutes), nightly batch and API-response-only, and aggregate retention as 24 months vs indefinite. Summary Art. 12(4) enhanced logging (biometric) is mis-applied to Area 5. Pinnacle is a maturity model, not an Act mapping (2/5; Domain 6 = 1), and expressly not legal advice.

8. BUDGET
Available EUR 800k plus 500k contingent (EUR 1.3m); EUR 95k spent. Only notified body (EUR 200-350k, premise doubtful) and logging (see section 4) are quantified. Full six-month raw logging is unaffordable; selective logging is the main cost lever. QMS, Annex IV, bias audit, instructions for use and adversarial testing are unestimated; obtain quotes before 31 March.

9. ROADMAP
Now (Feb-Mar 2025): litigation hold; FleetScore bias audit and NovaStar disclosure decision; vehicle-law reporting review of IR-2024-0847; confirm Annex I Section B treatment and the conformity route with approval authority; correct the summary (Section A/B, Annex III lettering, Art. 99, Art. 3(49)); AI literacy programme; Art. 5 contractual limits on NovaStar.
By Q2-Q3 2025: AI risk-management and QMS overlay; PedDetect data provenance and licence review; update OEM instructions (weather performance); adversarial testing plan before November 2025 v3.3 submission; event-based logging design.
By Omnibus-adjusted dates: Annex IV files, PMM plans, incident procedure, oversight design, human review of FleetScore premiums, ISO 9001 renewal with AI scope.
Unresolved: delegated-act status for 2019/2144; Omnibus OJ text; Art. 99/3(49)/Art. 19 wording; legality of the NovaStar data/age use.
